Pseudo chain volume series of a variable that changes sign

Source: R/chain_pseudo.R
chain_pseudo.Rd

Growth rates and chain volume measures cannot be calculated for variables that can take positive, negative and zero values, such as changes in inventories or the external trade balance (IMF QNA Manual, paragraph 8.56). The solution of the 2008 SNA (paragraphs 8.57 and 8.58) is to write the variable as the difference of two series that only take positive values, to chain-link each of them separately, and to take the difference of the chain volume measures. For instance, changes in inventories are closing inventories minus opening inventories, and the trade balance is exports minus imports.

Usage

chain_pseudo(
  cp_pos,
  pi_pos,
  cp_neg,
  pi_neg,
  method = c("ao", "oqo"),
  base_year = NULL
)

Arguments

cp_pos

Current prices of the series that takes positive values (ts; an mts is the aggregate of its columns): closing inventories, exports, etc.

pi_pos

Price indices of cp_pos over the previous year (previous year average = 100), with the same structure.

cp_neg, pi_neg

The same for the series that is subtracted (opening inventories, imports, etc.).

method

Chain-linking technique: "ao" for annual overlap, "oqo" for one-quarter overlap (for monthly series, the overlap period is the last month of the year).

base_year

Reference year (index = 100). By default, the year before the start of vo (or the first year of cp, if later).

Value

A ts: the chain volume measure (in monetary terms) of cp_pos minus the one of cp_neg.

Details

With \(x^{+}_t\) and \(x^{-}_t\) the chain volume measures of the two series (chain_laspeyres()), the pseudo chain volume series is \(x^{+}_t - x^{-}_t\).

The result is a pseudo chain volume series: it is the difference of two chained components, which are not additive by construction. It is expressed in monetary terms (its growth rates are meaningless). The measure of each series is that of chain_laspeyres().

If the two series are already chain-linked (in monetary terms, with the same reference year), their simple difference is the pseudo chain volume series.

References

International Monetary Fund (2018), Quarterly National Accounts Manual (2017 Edition), chapter 8 "Price and Volume Measures", Washington, DC. doi:10.5089/9781475589870.069 .

See also

chain_laspeyres(), chain_contrib()

Examples

# Illustration: the two products of the example 8.2 stand in for closing and
# opening inventories
chain_pseudo(imf_cp[, "A"], imf_pi[, "A"],
       imf_cp[, "B"], imf_pi[, "B"], base_year = 2010)
#>           Qtr1      Qtr2      Qtr3      Qtr4
#> 2011 -64.54248 -58.84171 -52.37369 -49.08110
#> 2012 -48.02250 -34.20406 -15.96712  30.79554
#> 2013  42.78602  67.23583  83.97240  92.08181
